reason: The decision guide quote states Reserved Instances are an older purchasing option generally recommended to be replaced with Savings Plans and that newer families might not support RI pricing.

The quotes state an instance that is too big or too small can be resized by changing its instance type and that Compute Optimizer can recommend the best type; the same page's table conditions an in-place change on compatibility.

The row supports migrating to a new instance type for an instance store root volume, but 'Not applicable' is the value of the Compatibility column, not a statement that an in-place type change is not applicable; the claim and the display reassign it.
The quote states a stop and start moves the instance to new hardware and a non-Elastic public IPv4 address is released and replaced with a new one.
Under the EBS-backed, compatible-type instructions the quotes state you must stop the instance before changing its type and must plan for downtime while it is stopped.
The quote states the type can be changed only if the current configuration is compatible, otherwise you launch a compatible new instance and migrate the application.
Under Architecture the quote states AMIs are specific to the processor architecture so you must select a type with the same architecture as the current type.
The quotes state irreparable host failure leads to a scheduled stop for an EBS root volume and a scheduled terminate for an instance store root volume.
The table row states the regional RI discount applies in any Availability Zone of the Region and the zonal RI discount only in the specified Availability Zone.
The table row states a regional RI does not reserve capacity and a zonal RI reserves capacity in the specified Availability Zone.
The table row states Standard RIs can't be exchanged and Convertible RIs can be exchanged during the term with new family, type, platform, scope or tenancy.
The quote states four attributes determine the price and the list in its context names instance type, Region, tenancy and platform.
The Limitations list states size flexibility is supported only for regional RIs and not for zonal, Windows, RHEL, SUSE or dedicated-tenancy RIs; the scope table confirms Linux/Unix default tenancy.
The quotes state RIs are a billing discount on matching running On-Demand Instances, applied immediately and automatically without a restart.
The restrictions list states at least one month remaining in the Standard RI term, at least 30 days active in the account, upfront payment received, and a minimum price of $0.00.
The quote states a service fee of 12 percent of the total upfront price of each Standard RI sold in the Marketplace.
The quote states after the sale you give up the capacity reservation and discounted fees and continued use is charged On-Demand from the time of sale.
The quotes state only Standard regional and zonal EC2 RIs can be sold and Convertible RIs can't be sold in the Marketplace.
The quote states RIs do not renew automatically and on expiry the instance continues without interruption at On-Demand rates.
The note states a successful billing history is required before you can purchase No Upfront RIs.

The table rows and examples support every listed factor, the two t2.small full coverage and the 50% t2.large case, but no quote says the factor 'doubles with each size step', and the same table continues 3xlarge 24, 6xlarge 48, so the rule is not general.
The quotes list All Upfront, Partial Upfront and No Upfront and state that generally a higher upfront payment saves more money.
The quote states a purchase cannot be cancelled, and its context says you might be able to modify, exchange or sell, depending on the offering class.
The quotes state the default of 80 new RIs per month in a three-AZ Region (20 regional plus 60 zonal) and that an instance count of 10 counts as 10, not 1.
The Default quota table row states 20 new regional RIs per Region per month; the page has a section on requesting a quota increase.
The Default quota table row states 20 new zonal RIs per Availability Zone per month; the page has a section on requesting a quota increase.
The quotes state the buyer determines the scope, regional or zonal, at purchase and that the scope does not affect the price.
The quotes state RI benefits are shared under one consolidated billing payer account and apply first to the purchasing account, then to other accounts in the organization.
The quote states flexibility uses the normalization factor, applies fully or partially to same-family instances in any AZ of the Region, and only family, tenancy and platform must match.
The quotes state Standard gives the most significant discount, can only be modified and can't be exchanged; Convertible gives a lower discount, can be exchanged and can be modified.
The quote states a one-year or three-year commitment, with the three-year commitment offering a bigger discount.
The quotes define one year as 31536000 seconds (365 days) and three years as 94608000 seconds (1095 days).
The tip states to right-size with Compute Optimizer before committing to a purchasing option because oversized instances waste money under any purchasing model.
The quote states a root volume is created at launch, contains the boot image, each instance has a single one, and storage can be added during or after launch.
The note states S3-backed AMIs are end of life, not recommended for new use, and supported only on C1, C3, D2, I2, M1, M2, M3, R3 and X1; the context says their root volume is instance store.

The quote states Compute Savings Plans apply regardless of Region, family, OS or tenancy and cover Fargate and Lambda, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to one family in a Region with higher discounts.
The FAQ quote states Savings Plans save like RIs but automatically reduce compute bills across any Region as usage changes, without exchanges or modifications.

The FAQ quote states Compute Savings Plans up to 66% like Convertible RIs across Region, family, size, OS, tenancy, Fargate and Lambda, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans up to 72% like Standard RIs within one family in a chosen Region.
The quotes state AWS can schedule reboot, stop and retire events, notifies by email in advance, and Auto Scaling eventually replaces an affected instance through health checks.
The quote states that, unlike primary private IP addresses, secondary private IP addresses can be reassigned from one instance to another.
